key_insight: Wall-resolved LES shows that a 10% chord spanwise domain can capture the main transition physics of a wind-turbine airfoil, including a Kelvin-Helmholtz wavepacket in the laminar separation bubble and a slow low-frequency force oscillation.
engineering_relevance: The results help validate lower-cost CFD settings for wind-turbine airfoil transition prediction and identify operating conditions where periodic stall/reattachment or bubble bursting may affect loads and fatigue.
method: Wall-resolved LES with Nek5000 and EllipSys at Re_c = 1e5 and AoA = 3.1°–3.3°
Spectral proper orthogonal decomposition (SPOD) to extract dominant disturbance mode shapes
Comparison with parabolized stability equation (PSE) results and long-time force histories
evidence_signal: EllipSys matches Nek5000 closely for mean flow and most perturbation growth, while long-time simulations show a 10.5% normal-force modulation with period 48 flow-through times.
watch_item: EllipSys underpredicts Tollmien-Schlichting wave amplitude due to higher numerical dissipation, so near-wall transition predictions may remain sensitive to solver choice and resolution.
paper_title: Numerical simulations of transition and long-term response of a wind turbine airfoil
